title: The End of Faith and the Presence of Prophets
english: And I will know just as I was known. You see, that it will be abolished for the better; and what is that? When those who believe are present, faith will cease. For we no longer believe, but we see. But faith seen is no longer faith. For whatever one sees, what also does he believe? And this is it: for we see now through a mirror in a riddle (1 Cor 13:12), but then face to face. Then, when then? It is clear, when the end [comes].

{M.} Behold, therefore, Montanus the Paraclete has come and has given us the perfection. {O.} The perfection, when it comes, will it be abolished in part or not? {M.} Thus it has been written. {O.} But we see that Montanus is being abolished until today; but the [things] of the holy Paul are increasing. {M.} And indeed you also abolish the [things] of Paul, saying that after Christ there is no prophet.

{O.} You wander, not knowing the Scriptures nor what the Church teaches. For we know that even after Christ there are prophets. For Jesus himself said: 'Behold, I will send to you prophets and wise men and scribes, and from them you will kill and crucify and from them you will scourge in your synagogues' (Matt 23:2-3). And Paul says: 'Earnestly desire the greater gifts, and above all, that you may prophesy' (1 Cor 14:1). And again he says: 'If then the whole church comes together and all speak in tongues, and there comes in an unlearned man or an unbeliever, will they not say that you are out of your minds? But if all prophesy, and there comes in an unbeliever or an unlearned man, he is convicted by all, examined by all, the secrets of his heart become manifest to all, and so falling on his face he will worship God, declaring that truly God is in our midst' (1 Cor 14:23-26).

{M.} How then do you say that after Christ no one became a prophet? {O.} We also after Christ confess that prophets have come to be, and that they have even the apostles and the gift of prophecy.
